But the traditional methods could not compute the path vector correspond to diffraction ray tube when ray which ray tube intersect with the obstacle such as furniture. In this paper, a novel diffracted tubes technology has been put forword, which can effectively overcome the shortcoming of traditional method and the diffracted tube path vector expression has been calculated. According to the novel method, none of the diffraction tubes which is contributed to the receiver is given up. As the result, the prediction efficiency can be improved.

articleTitle: A novel variable inductor using a triple transformer and MOS switches in 0.13 μm CMOS technology
abstract: This paper presents a novel variable inductor consisting of a triple transformer, pMOSFET switches and a level shift circuit in 0.13 μm CMOS technology. The structure of the variable inductor is designed and analyzed by using Ansoft HFSS. The inductance varies from 0.678 nH to 1.055 nH with changing a control voltage from 0 to 1.5 V. The quality factor of the variable inductor is around 7 at 3.4 GHz.

articleTitle: An improvement of strip-coaxial transition with ultra-broadband
abstract: A method of ultra-broadband strip-coaxial transition is described in this paper to settle connection problem. Decreasing the width of strip-line at strip-coaxial transition junction is adopted in the transition structure to eliminate the discontinuousness and gain an ultra-broadband with 1~18 GHz (vswr<;1.05 and loss<;0.06dB). An example is analyzed and simulated. The method is applied in 2-ways power divider to validate the design validity and a good performance is gained.

articleTitle: A novel microwave equalizer using substrate integrated waveguide concept
abstract: A novel scheme for designing microwave equalizer based on Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) is investigated with simulation and experiment. Compared with the classical equalizers that developed by the microstrip, the new equalizer have the advantages such as high Q-factor and low radiation losses etc. Additionally, since the SIW have small size than the corresponding conventional rectangular waveguide components, it can easily be integrated with other microwave circuits in the same substrate. Hence it's a good choice to use SIW for the developing of the novel microwave equalizer.

articleTitle: High-gain thinned array with limited scan capability
abstract: A high-gain thinned array with limited scan capability is proposed, in which sub-arrays are vertically mounted as the elements. The technique can be easily applied to the phased radar systems, and therefore decrease the cost and weight.

articleTitle: A suspended stripline dual-band filter using inter-digitally coupled resonator pairs
abstract: This paper presents a design of suspended stripline dual-band filter, in which, inter-digitally coupled resonator pairs act as dual-mode resonators to realize the two passbands. Parallel coupling is adopted between adjacent dual-mode resonators and the input/output couplings are realized using tapped lines of certain height. A prototype dual-band filter with two bands located at 2.4 and 5.2GHz is designed and fabricated. Advantages of low insertion loss and high in-between isolation are observed by the measurement. To adjust the ratio of bandwidths, an improved dual-band coupling schematic is given with simulated results presented.

articleTitle: A SiGe HBT low noise variable gain amplifier with controllable feedback of a p-i-n diode
abstract: A low noise amplifier with dB-linear variable gain has been designed and fabricated based on high performance SiGe HBT in this paper. Negative feedback technology has been adopted to change the transmission gain of HBT through variable resistance of a forward biased p-i-n diode in the feedback path. The simulation results and measurement results agree well in frequency of 1.8GHz for CDMA application. A dynamic gain control of 14 dB in a control voltage range of 0.6–3.0 V has been achieved through the controllable feedback of the p-i-n diode. The noise figure was always lower than 5.5dB when the controlled voltage changed and the minimum noise figure is about 2.6dB. Both input matching and output matching maintained constants under all controlled voltage points.

articleTitle: In-orbit verification of a compact Ku-band transmitter for a Pico-satellite
abstract: Outline and in-orbit verification of a Ku-band transmitter installed in a Pico-satellite are described. We had successfully caught telemetry signals after eleven days of the satellite launch. Despite of a limited operation period, we have confirmed that a specially developed Ku-band transmitter was survived in space environment during eighteen days.

articleTitle: Observation of reverse Doppler effect in a composite right/left-handed transmission line
abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate the reverse Doppler effect associated with the left-handed medium by a simple transmission line circuit implantation. The left-handed medium is analogized with the composite right/left-handed transmission line at microwave frequency. Virtual moving source is realized in the composite right/left-handed medium by electrically trigged voltage-controlled sequential switching of transmission-line taps along the transmission line. By analyzing the frequency spectrum of the output signals, we found that the frequency shift supported the reverse Doppler effect in such left-handed transmission line system.

articleTitle: Compact band-notched UWB BPF with enhanced pass-band characteristic
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for designing compact band-notch ultra-wideband (UWB) bandpass filter with a good enhanced pass-band characteristic. Notch-band and enhanced pass-band characteristic are obtained by using the radial-cross loaded stub at the same time. The main advantage of the proposed filter is the pass-band can be expanding to including the whole WLAN band. Equivalent model is given depending on the odd/even excitation resonance condition. The characteristics of the filter are analyzed. To verify the proposed methods, filter is designed and fabricated. Measured results show the proposed UWB properties from 2.2 to 10.4 GHz and the notch band can be changed optionally from 4GHz to 7GHz. These filters can be integrated in UWB radio systems and efficiently enhance the interference immunity from undesired signals such as wireless local area network (WLAN) and WiMAX.

articleTitle: A neural network model of silicon-based millimeter-wave coplanar waveguide
abstract: In this paper, neural network modeling techniques are presented for millimeter-wave modeling of silicon-based millimeter-wave coplanar waveguide. The neural network is trained to learn the mapping between the geometrical variables and S parameter of the coplanar waveguide. Once trained with the EM data, this model provides accurate and fast prediction of the measurement data of differential CPW with geometry parameters as variables. Experiments in comparison with input-output relationships by the proposed neural network model and measurement data are included to demonstrate the merits of this new model.

articleTitle: Bandstop filters of suspended stripline design using the quasi-lumped element approach
abstract: In this paper, bandstop filters of suspended stripline are proposed. The filters are a ladder circuit structure which has the shunt-circuit modules in the series branches and the series-circuit ones in the ladder's shunt arms. Each of these individual modules provides a transmission zero whose frequency can be independently tuned. Two bandstop filters are built from utilizing three and five of these zero-generating circuit modules, respectively. The rejection bandwidth is dominated by the distribution of the zeros. The quasi-lumped elements circuit model is developed to analyze the circuit performance and the experiments are conducted to verify the filters' design.

articleTitle: The predicted technique of EMI for ship radars based on the GTD revision
abstract: The prediction from classic prediction equation on EMI is revised with GTD which can quantify analysis the effect against transmission on obscuration from superstructure of ship. In addition, quantified diffraction factor and diffraction loss are obtained. It can correct the defect of traditional method which ignores the obscuration from superstructure of ship (or only qualitative analysis). And the new EMI prediction method on ship radars has been developed, it will lend deep-seated technical support to full improving EMC of ship.

articleTitle: A miniaturized planar UWB antenna with a trapezoid shape ground
abstract: A miniaturized planar UWB (Ultra Wide Band) antenna implemented on a FR-4 substrate is proposed in this paper. The antenna uses a tapered microstrip line as a feed line, and has 1-stage trapezoid shape ground. Its total size is 25 × 30 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The antenna proposed in this paper is much smaller than the antenna using a uniform feed line and a conventional square ground. It is also smaller than the UWB antenna we proposed last year. The simulated and measured results on impedance matching, radiation pattern and time domain characteristic over UWB band are given.

articleTitle: Analysis of compact circularly-polarized patch antenna with bent slots using MoM
abstract: Input and radiation characteristics of compact circularly-polarized (CP) patch antenna with bent slots using in the microsatellite formation flying is analyzed by the method of moments (MoM) in this paper. Firstly, the CP antenna with finite ground plane is simulated by the MoM based on the Schaubert-Wilton-Glisson (SWG) basis function. Then effects of several antenna design parameters, including bent-slot length, bent-slot width, patch length, corner width, and feeding point position, on reflection coefficient and radiation pattern are studied. Finally, the performance of this antenna is compared with the conventional one.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic compatibility design of terminal system for vehicle
abstract: In accordance with systematic structure and function, this thesis analyzes the factors causing electromagnetic interference and the principal transmitting ways of EMI. Based on which, together with a combination of the shielding skill and ESD protection skill, detailed hardware design and anti-interference measures are given.

articleTitle: A new coupling method for quarter-wave coaxial cavity resonator used for sterilization
abstract: In this paper, a new coupling method for the quarter-wave coaxial cavity resonator is proposed and designed for sterilization. The inner and outer conductors of the quarter-wave coaxial cavity is connected by two symmetrical inductive bend metallic stubs to achieve zero-voltage at the lower end of the resonator. The upper end forms an open circuit and the voltage has its maximum. Compared with other traditional coupling structures, such as loop coupling, this type of structure not only keeps good performance in simple configuration, but also has many additional advantages. For example, it can be integrated and fabricated with the conventional quarter-wave coaxial cavity resonator together to improve the fabrication accuracy and operation reliability. Besides, it has high repeatability and mass-producibility. The detailed design process is introduced in this paper. The proposed coupling structure and the corresponding quarter-wave coaxial cavity resonator are modeled, analyzed and simulated by the commercial software HFSS. The electric field near the upper end of the inner conductor can reach 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> V/m, so it is sufficient to break the cell membrane and be used for sterilization. This simple and effective coupling method and the corresponding integrated resonator can be employed in the plasma excitation and dielectric measurement applications as well.

articleTitle: Wide band antenna for mobile devices
abstract: A wide band antenna composed of two stubs and a ground is proposed. The antenna has more-series resonant frequencies than an open and a short stub, and there for it achieves wide-band operation. A prototype of this antenna is designed, fabricated and measured. The prototype has over twice wider frequency band where good radiation efficiency is maintained than a conventional low profile antenna. The width of the prototype is 75mm, height is 10mm, thickness is 1mm and radiation efficiency is over -3.1dB from 0.7GHz to 0.96GHz.

articleTitle: A compact filter with resonating-irises and shorting stubs
abstract: This paper presents a filter with resonating-irises and shorting stubs. Each shorting stub not only creates a transmission zero, but also serves as the impedance inverter between adjacent resonating-irises, to form the bandpass filter. Transmission zeros (TZs) at both sides of the passband of a broadband as well as a narrow band filter can be realized. The configuration parameters and simulated results are presented. Tested results agree well with the simulation results. The length of the sample filter is less than 20% of a directly-coupled waveguide filter with the same specifications.

articleTitle: A novel E-plane half-mode substrate integrated waveguide (HMSIW) coupler
abstract: A novel E-plane 3 dB directional coupler has been proposed and developed in multilayer HMSIW topology. A continuous coupling slot is etched in the center conductor layer at the magnetic-wall of HMSIW. Design process is introduced based on the even-odd mode theory. As a promising technology, the developed HMSIW E-plane coupler inherits those merits of low profile, low insertion loss, low lost and good compatibility with planar transmission lines etc. Additionally, more compact design has been achieved than H-plane HMSIW coupler.

articleTitle: Design of waveguide to suspended microstrip probe transition at terahertz atmospheric window
abstract: The terahertz (THz) region of the electromagnetic spectrum, spanning from 100 GHz through 10 THz, become more and more import for a wide range scientific, military and commercial applications day by day. This paper presents a design of novel waveguide to suspended microstrip probe transition at terahertz atmospheric window 220GHz using sector step impedance matching circuit by Advanced Design System (ADS) and High Frequency Simulation System (HFSS). Simulation results show transition bandwidth about 20% from 200GHz to 240GHz (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> below -15dB, S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub> below -0.2dB).

articleTitle: Resonant-mode behavior of a new slotline-embedded three-mode microstrip-line resonator and its filter application
abstract: This paper presents detailed investigations on resonant-mode behavior of a new three-mode resonator, which consists of a parallel-coupled microstrip line resonator embedded with a slotline resonator. Electric-field distributions and modal resonant frequencies of three modes are analyzed by using an electromagnetic simulator, thereby showing that the three modes are controllable with the ratio of the microstrip-line length to the slotline length. Based on the results of the resonant-mode behavior, a very compact bandpass filter and its circuit model are developed to confirm the effectiveness of the resonator. The developed filter has three reflection zeros in the passband and four transmission zeros near the passband as well as a sharp skirt property and a wide stopband. The validity of the multipole response is supported by the calculated results of the circuit model formed by a multi-path configuration.

articleTitle: A wideband integrated Gilbert cell mixer with an inductor resonator using 0.5um GaAs enhancement-mode pHEMT technology
abstract: A fully integrated active Gilbert cell mixer with inductor resonator was proposed in this paper. The proposed circuit was designed at 12 GHz with bandwidth from 5 to 20 GHz and fabricated in a 0.5-μm pHEMT process. An extra inductor was added to enhance the conversion gain and improve the noise figure. The “current bleeding” technique was also inserted in the Gilbert cell mixer to boost the conversion gain, meanwhile, improving the noise level. The highest conversion gain of 11 dB can be achieved in the designed circuit under LO input power of 4.5 dBm. Both RF-IF and LO-IF isolations were better than 30dB. The third order intercept point input power, IIP3, achieved as high as 6 dBm. Total consumption is 59.6 mW. The total chip area is 1.15 * 0.92 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Digital predistortion for power amplifiers with memory effects
abstract: Power amplifier is essential component in communication systems and it's inherently nonlinear. This essay mainly investigate a based on Hammerstein predistorter, a memory polynomial predistorter. The Hammerstein predistorter is designed specifically for power amplifiers that can be modeled as a Wiener system. The memory polynomial predistorter can correct both the nonlinear distortions and the linear frequency response that may exist in the power amplifier.

articleTitle: Analysis of two-arm conical log-spiral antennas using FE-BI method
abstract: Radiation properties of two-arm conical log-spiral antennas (CLSA) are analyzed by using the finite element and boundary integral equation hybrid method (FE-BI) in the paper. Firstly the radiation performances of the CLSA with same structure parameters and different frequencies are simulated. Then the impacts of wrap angle and cone angle on radiation properties are calculated in detail. Simulated results show that the geometry parameters of a CLSA greatly affect its radiation properties, but for the same geometry parameters, CLSA possess wider frequency band. Therefore structure parameters should be carefully optimized in practical applications.

articleTitle: Design of a Low Noise Amplifier with integrated notch filter for interference rejection in ultra-wideband systems
abstract: A fully integrated 0.18um CMOS Low Noise Amplifier (LNA) with Notch Filter for interference rejection at 5-6 GHz in UWB systems is presented. The notch filter comprises a series LC resonance circuit, which with a resistance cancelation approach yields excellent attenuating characteristics. The post layout simulation of this circuit is able to achieve more than 25 dB of attenuation at 5.6 GHz. The LNA is composed of two stages-cascode and cascade stage, in addition to inter-stage LC components to achieve wider gain. The shunt resistive feedback is employed to obtain a good input matching and low noise figure. The proposed UWB LNA achieves a simulated (post layout) gain of 18 dB and has the input and output matching less than -7dB and -10dB respectively over the entire range. The NF in the region of interest is less than 5.1 dB.

articleTitle: Design of low power up-conversion self-oscillating mixer
abstract: A 5 GHz up-conversion self-oscillating mixer (SOM) for IEEE 802.11j WLAN transmitter, fabricated using CMOS 0.18μm process, is presented in this paper. The conversion gain of the proposed mixer is mainly boosted by current-bleeding technique which can achieve high gain under less power consumption. To enhance the transconductance, the proposed voltage controlled oscillator (VCO) employs a complementarily cross-coupled architecture. Under 1.4V and 1.2V supply voltage of Mixer and VCO, respectively, the measured results of the proposed Mixer reveal a conversion gain of 9.1dB, input third-order intercept (IIP3) of -8dBm, phase noise of -116.7dBc/Hz at 1 MHz offset and tuning range of 4.41GHz~5.08GHz (13.34%) while total power consumption is only 9.2mW. The size of the chip is 1.06mm ×1.12mm.

articleTitle: Design of local oscillator for digital trunking communication
abstract: In this paper, the configuration of ADF4350 and high performance of Phase-Locked Loop (PLL) chip are briefly introduced. The design of a stable local oscillator signal generator circuit module is applied to the system of Digital Trunking Communication System. The main hardware circuit and simulation data of Voltage Control Oscillator (VCO) are involved in the paper and the result is correct basically.

articleTitle: Design and research of clothing management RFID tag
abstract: We researched the design for RFID tag's antenna of clothing management in this paper, and encapsulation materials how to influence the quality of label, we also analyzed how to select the encapsulation materials. The paper describes the performance parameters and characteristic of the label at the end. This article focuses on the design of encapsulation materials and tries to provide practical advice of clothing management RFID tag's design.

articleTitle: A dual-frequency triangular planar inverted-F antenna with U-shaped sleeves
abstract: It is presented a single-feed dual-frequency triangular Planar Inverted-F Antenna with U-shaped sleeves in this paper. A shorting-wall and a V-shaped slot are introduced to enhance the bandwidths in lower operating and higher operating frequency respectively. For return loss (S11) ≤−10dB, a relative bandwidth of more than 25% (2.1GHz–2.7GHz) at lower operating frequency and of more than 19.3% (4.9GHz–5.95GHz) at higher operating frequency can be achieved, which can satisfy the IEEE 802.11 WLAN standards in the 2.4 GHz (2400–2484 MHz)/5.2 GHz (5150–5350 MHz)/5.8 GHz (5725–5825 MHz) operating bands.

articleTitle: A 2.12∼2.68GHz wide tuning CMOS LC-VCO with low phase noise
abstract: A wideband LC voltage-control oscillator (VCO) is designed based on SMIC 0.18μm CMOS process, which has wide tuning range by using the switched capacitor array, while the phase noise is reduced after using the differential inductance of high quality factor and the filter method. Simulated results show that the VCO has the tuning range of 23.3% from 2.12GHz to 2.68GHz, and the phase noise of -128.1dBc/Hz at offset of 1MHz from a 2.4GHz carrier. With a 1.8V supply voltage, the power of core circuit is 6.9mW.

articleTitle: A novel method of designing chaotic spread-spectrum sequence based on combined Tent-map
abstract: This paper proposes a novel method of designing chaotic spread-spectrum sequence based on combined Tent-map. The presented combined sequence is almost uniformly distributed over (0, 1), while the traditional chaotic sequences are far away from uniform distribution. Computer experiments show that the combined chaotic sequences are capable of passing the strict Diehard randomness tests, which provides the evidence of their robustness in statistical properties.

articleTitle: Analysis of periodic structures with GPU accelerating
abstract: Various FDTD approaches has been applied in the analysis of periodic structures, among which Spectral FDTD is a straight-forward and robust one. This essay proposed an improved Spectral FDTD algorithm that improves the simulation speed of off-normal incident case without jeopardizing accuracy. Together with GPU accelerating, as is proven by the example, the proposed acceleration scheme offers a speedup of 22 at minimum.

articleTitle: Performance improvement in phase-modulation radio over fiber link through carrier suppression using stimulated Brillouin scattering
abstract: A simple and low-cost method for improving RF performance in phase modulation radio-over-fiber (RoF) systems by using stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) is proposed and demonstrated. We present a simple analytical model to assess the relationship between performance improvement of the phase-modulation RoF link and the carrier suppression ratio x. The experiment results show good agreement with the theory.

articleTitle: Compact ultra-wideband directional printed antenna with notched band
abstract: A compact printed log-periodic dipole antenna (CPLPDA) with a notched band is proposed for ultra-wideband (UWB) applications. The width of the largest dipole is reduced with the method of folding the dipole arms, and capacitive rectangular patches are loaded at the end of the arms for further reducing the size. A notched band is generated by integrating a U-shaped slot into the CPLPDA for anti-jamming purpose. The impedance bandwidth with VSWR less than 2 is from 3.1GHz to 10.6 GHz. The measured results are in agreement with the simulated results.
